title: Stability gates: auto-rerun on p95 variance threshold + flaky-run CI coverage
author: Rina Kobayashi
description: Context: We’re seeing run-to-run instability in p95 latency on some model/region pairs (queueing effects, transient noisy neighbors, kernel selection differences). This PR adds a stability gate to the benchmark pipeline that detects high variance in p95 latency and automatically re-runs the affected slice up to a bounded limit. Goal: reduce noise in published aggregates while preserving the raw evidence trail (we keep the original run results and annotate what happened). What’s included: (1) Variance detection on repeated trials for each (model, region, workload, concurrency) slice, based on p95 latency. (2) Auto rerun when variance exceeds a configurable threshold, with a cap on reruns and explicit status reporting. (3) Manifest + result artifacts include stability metadata (variance %, trials, rerun_count, stability_status, stability_notes). (4) CI coverage: simulated flaky runs with deterministic jitter to ensure the gate triggers and produces stable, explainable output. Default behavior: run N trials (default N=5) per slice; compute p95 per trial; compute variance metric = (max(p95)-min(p95))/median(p95). If variance_metric > threshold (default 0.08 = 8%), schedule rerun for that slice, up to max_reruns (default 2). If still unstable after max reruns, mark slice as UNSTABLE and keep it in output with stability_status=UNSTABLE (so downstream publish steps can choose to exclude or flag it explicitly). Config: new runner flags --stability-trials, --stability-threshold, --stability-max-reruns, --stability-disable (for local debugging). Notes: This does not change the latency/$ computation; it only governs which trials are considered stable and how reruns are executed/recorded. Follow-ups: integrate with region sweep runner to prioritize reruns in the same reservation window; wire stability_status into the publish checklist (Confluence validation checklist) so Marketing only pulls STABLE slices for public tables unless explicitly approved.

conversation: Jonas Weber (review): I like the direction, but please make sure we don’t silently ‘fix’ bad numbers. We should (a) keep original trials, (b) cap reruns, and (c) clearly mark UNSTABLE when we hit the cap. Also: can we choose a variance metric that is easy to explain to non-ML folks? Rina (author): Agree. Updated to always persist per-trial p95s, added stability_status=UNSTABLE when max_reruns exceeded, and changed metric to (max-min)/median which is easier to describe than CV. Claire Dubois (review): Two asks: (1) add a --stability-disable flag for debugging, (2) ensure rerun slices keep the same prompt set seed (we can’t let rerun change workload distribution). Rina: Added --stability-disable and pinned the prompt_set_seed into the slice key; reruns reuse the same seed and prompt indices. Nadia Rahman (review): Make sure the rerun logic doesn’t alter the cost attribution window. Some of our $/token normalization assumes fixed sampling. Also please add a note to the manifest so downstream knows which trials are ‘counted’ in the aggregate. Rina: Rerun doesn’t touch cost accounting; it only changes which trial set is used for the aggregated p95. Added manifest fields counted_trial_ids and stability_notes explaining selection. Sean Gallagher (review): CI coverage is good; please ensure flaky simulation test is deterministic and won’t cause CI to intermittently fail. Also add a small timeout guard so rerun planning can’t explode runtime if something is consistently unstable. Rina: Flaky sim uses fixed RNG seed; added runtime guard: max_total_attempts per job and early abort with UNSTABLE status if exceeded. Jonas (final): Looks good. Please add one more doc line recommending threshold ranges for different workloads. Rina: Added guidance (5–10% typical, 12% for high concurrency stress). Approved.
